---
title: "Cohort-driven, assay-aware thalassaemia genotyping"
abstract: |
  This thesis combines a retrospective molecular-testing study with an explicit
  computational model of ONT amplicon observability. The clinical study defines
  the locally relevant HBA/HBB genotype and phenotype questions. NanoGlobin
  compiles declared primer designs against chromosome-haplotype sequences,
  classifies observed molecules, and ranks the diploid haplotype states that can
  explain those products. Accuracy claims are restricted to the scope of each
  independent truth source; caller concordance is reported separately.
---

source("R/setup.R")

# Research question

Can a canonical chromosome-haplotype and evidence representation unify
retrospective thalassaemia records, support genotype--phenotype and database
analyses, expose assay-dependent blind spots, and drive an open ONT amplicon
genotyper?

```text
historical and ONT reports
    -> canonical genotype and evidence ledger
    -> reported HBA/HBB landscape and HBA x HBB phenotype analysis
    -> sequence-resolved candidate haplotypes
    -> declared assay compiler
    -> primer-aware molecule evidence
    -> chromosome-haplotype posterior
    -> resolved, ambiguous, or no-call
    -> independent adjudication
```

# Evidence available in this checkout

The repository contains real, aggregate HPRC/GIAB small-variant result records,
DRAGEN-labelled HBA comparator observations, public amplicon run metadata and the
measured Cython replacement benchmark. Patient-level reports and governed cohort
tables are not committed. Consequently, this book renders the software-method and
evaluation chapters from committed evidence but does not invent cohort results.
